disease_label_per_paper: Blast crisis of chronic myeloid leukemia with der(16)t(1;16)(q12;q11.2), B-lymphoid crisis, and DIC during presentation course
presentation_summary: 70-year-old man with known CML treated with imatinib and dasatinib was admitted after several weeks of fatigue and dyspnea.
Admission labs showed WBC 287,060/uL with 90% blasts, hemoglobin 6.3 g/dL, platelets 5.6 x10^4/uL, LDH 929 U/L, uric acid 9.6 mg/dL, CRP 8.81 mg/dL, D-dimer 6.84, and fibrinogen 367 mg/dL.
The patient's symptoms quickly worsened and he developed DIC; peripheral blood and cytogenetic testing confirmed CML blast crisis with additional chromosomal abnormality.

confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: reciprocal translocation of chromosomes 9 and 22; FISH of bcr and abl1

outcome: Blasts disappeared from peripheral blood 15 days after chemotherapy; discharged and continued ponatinib without progression at the report's follow-up.
quality_warnings: BCR-ABL, cytogenetics, and blast lineage are confirmatory/context only.
Admission laboratory values are retained as ordinary observations; DIC is course evidence because it developed after symptoms quickly worsened.
